restrictions: Generic, distribution-free birthday attack; uses no structural property of 32-round SHA-256 and produces no concrete collision.
Complete analytic candidate; charged time is a worst-case upper bound over the algorithm's own coins, not a full-scale execution.

Each of the q records stores three 256-bit words (digest, u, v); the per-record cost charges the packed compression, the digest transpose, the message-identity transpose that materializes (u, v), the record store, the loop-control overhead of every non-unrolled record- and bucket-proportional pass, and the counting-sort grouping over the three-word records; the proof enumerates every cost-model primitive category and shows each is charged.

The compression gate count is charged on the fully hand-derivable UNFOLDED basis (64,416 compression+digest gates), matched to the last gate by an inlined instrumented counter; every loop has a compile-time-fixed trip count with no data-dependent branch, so the total is exactly (per-record count) times q, an identity rather than an extrapolation from the verified batches.

Declared time_log2 = 126.1 is a conservative upper bound over all register-rich accountings including the per-bit-plane rotation surcharge (126.075); the pessimistic four-ops-per-gate memory model gives 127.542 (127.665 with the surcharge), all below the prior generic exponent 128.22.
